title: Add quote-aware YAML comment stripping to prevent silent matching failures
context: The indexer matches K8s resource names across files using a 'no match → no edge, never guess' strategy. When YAML values contain inline comments (e.g., `name: my-config  # app settings`), the comment was folded into the value text. This broke matching: the commented name never matched the same resource's uncommented reference elsewhere, producing a silent false negative (no edge) that is indistinguishable from correct conservatism—the worst failure mode. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Implement `stripTrailingComment()` that removes trailing `#` comments only when they appear after whitespace at value boundaries, while preserving `#` inside quoted strings and Sprig template expressions (e.g., `{{ .x | default "#fff" }}`). Apply this before value classification in K8s manifest extraction.
consequences: Values like `my-config  # note` now correctly normalize to `my-config` and match their uncommented references
The 'no match → no edge' guarantee is restored; silent matching failures are eliminated
Quote-aware stripping prevents loss of legitimate `#` characters in values
Matching becomes deterministic: the same resource seen with or without an inline comment produces identical identity
alternatives_rejected: Strip all `#` characters (would break quoted and templated values containing `#`)
Document the comment-matching issue as user responsibility (would leave silent failures unfixed)
Use regex-only stripping without quote state tracking (would produce false positives)
